Criterion: Verify the safe installation of the fuel system and components. Standard: Fuel components and plumbing withstand expected loading conditions for all phases of flight for static and durability related loads as well as internal pressure loads. Adequate brackets and clamps are provided for the expected conditions. Method of Compliance: Component performance is validated through qualification testing. System performance is validated through simulator and air vehicle testing. Inspections of fuel system plumbing and component installations after air vehicle operation confirm appropriate clearance and support. Installation integrity is confirmed by on-aircraft system-level proof pressure test. References: JSSG-2009: 3.3.3.1, 4.3.3.1, 3.3.8, 4.3.8 MIL-F-17874 14 CFR 23.963, 23.993, 23.994, 25.963, 25.993, 25.994, 27.963, 27.993, 29.963, 29.993

Standard: Fuel components, plumbing, tanks, and support structures withstand all expected loading conditions, including all operations for static, dynamic, durability related loads in combination with all internal pressure loads, and ground loads. This includes loads resulting from fuel slosh, vibration, relative movement from fuel lines and fittings, fuel system operation, expected pressure changes, and thermal stress. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct structural analysis that shows the fuel system and support structures will not fail under all operating conditions, including all static, dynamic, and durability related loads, in combination with all internal pressure loads and ground loads. Test.
  (1) Ground test: Conduct air vehicle system-level proof testing to verify installation integrity.
  (2) Ground test: Conduct ground tests that validate analysis that shows the fuel tanks and components can withstand all ground and flight conditions and environments.
  (3) Ground test: Conduct ground tests to show that pressure and thermal relief features maintain pressures within design limits. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (4) Flight test: Conduct post-flight inspections to verify required clearance, support, and installation integrity have been maintained.
  (5) Flight test: Conduct flight test to show that the fuel tanks can withstand all flight conditions and environments.
  (6) Flight test: Conduct flight tests to verify that pressure and thermal relief features maintain pressures within design limits.
